title: Give paid sick leave
summary: Businesses with 15 or more employees must give paid sick and safe leave: at least 1 hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year. Size is the average monthly number of employees in the prior calendar year, counting part-time, temporary, and seasonal workers.
action: Track leave for each employee, put your leave policy in writing, and display the state's sick and safe leave poster. A paid time off policy that gives at least as much leave also counts.
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Sick and Safe Leave FAQs

title: Give sick leave (it can be unpaid)
summary: Businesses with fewer than 15 employees must still let employees earn sick and safe leave (at least 1 hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year), but it can be unpaid. Size is the average monthly number of employees in the prior calendar year, counting part-time workers.
action: Track leave for each employee and follow the same tracking and notice rules as larger employers. You may choose to make the leave paid.
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Sick and Safe Leave FAQs

title: Allow up to 6 weeks of unpaid parental leave
summary: Employers with 15 to 49 employees in Maryland must give eligible employees up to 6 weeks of unpaid leave for the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child. Since October 1, 2025, employers covered by the federal FMLA are exempt.
action: Add parental leave to your written policies. If you're not sure whether the federal FMLA covers you, check with the U.S. Department of Labor.
verify: six (6) workweeks of unpaid parental leave
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Leave laws (Parental Leave); SB 785 (2025), Chapter 296

title: Don't ask about criminal records before the first interview
summary: Employers with 15 or more full-time employees in Maryland can't ask applicants about criminal records (on the application or otherwise) before the first in-person interview. Phone and video interviews count as in-person.
action: Remove criminal record questions from your job applications and early screening.
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Criminal Record Screening (Ban the Box) FAQs

title: Don't require employees to attend political or religious meetings
summary: Starting October 1, 2026, employers can't punish employees for refusing to attend or take part in employer meetings about religious or political matters. The state must publish a poster and model notice by November 1, 2026.
action: Make any such meetings optional. Once the state's poster is out, post it where employees can see it and give the notice to each new hire.

deadlines.label: Post the state's Worker Freedom Act poster (state publishes it by this date)

frequencyNote: Plus a notice to each new hire

title: Pay at least the Maryland minimum wage[[ ({{wage.state}} an hour)]]
summary: Most employees in Maryland must be paid at least the state minimum wage[[, currently {{wage.state}} per hour]]. Employees under 18 must get at least 85% of it. Some jobs are exempt. Overtime is 1.5 times the regular rate after 40 hours a week.
action: Check that every employee earns at least the state minimum wage[[ of {{wage.state}}]] and display the state minimum wage poster.
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Minimum Wage and Overtime Law

title: Tipped staff: follow the tipped wage rules[[ ({{wage.stateTipped}} an hour plus tips)]]
summary: For tipped employees (more than $30 a month in tips), you must pay at least the tipped cash wage[[ of {{wage.stateTipped}} per hour]], and that plus tips must reach the full minimum wage. You cover any gap. Restaurants using tips toward minimum wage must give a Tip Credit Wage Statement each pay period.
action: Check each pay period that cash wage plus tips reaches the minimum wage, and give tipped staff their wage statement. In counties with their own minimum wage, check the county's tipped-wage rules.
verify: earning more than $30 per month in tips
sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Minimum Wage and Overtime Law

title: Report each new hire to the state within 20 days
summary: Maryland employers must report every newly hired or rehired employee to the Maryland State Directory of New Hires within 20 days. The state uses the reports for child support and unemployment insurance checks. Missing reports can be fined.
action: Report each new or rehired employee within 20 days of hire.
agency: Maryland Department of Human Services, Child Support Administration
verify: report newly hired or rehired employees within 20 days

title: Put up the MOSH safety poster and report serious injuries
summary: Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) requires employers to post the MOSH poster where employees will see it. Report any work-related death to MOSH within 8 hours, and any in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye within 24 hours.
action: Download the free MOSH poster and put it up in a prominent place. Save MOSH's phone number for injury reports.
verify: Post, at a prominent location within the workplace, the MOSH Poster

title: Keep an injury and illness log (OSHA Form 300)
summary: Employers with more than 10 employees must keep a log of work-related injuries and illnesses and post the yearly summary (Form 300A) from February 1 to April 30. Some low-hazard industries are partly exempt, so check whether yours is.
action: Check if your industry is exempt. If not, keep Form 300 up to date and post Form 300A each February 1 through April 30.
frequencyNote: Log ongoing; post the summary Feb 1 to Apr 30
